comment: Dr. Simpson is a great lab professor for Pchem. He is a super witty guy who makes sure you know exactly how to do the lab before having to do it, and although he has high expectations for your excels and lab write-ups, he is willing to check over them before submitting to ensure you have everything correct. Best ponytail ever too.

Very smart, knows what he's talking about. Sometimes it can be hard to understand his explanations if you've never taken chem before. However, he'll tell you exactly what you need to know for quizzes. Def visit in office hours, he'll work through problems and answer any and all questions. Lectures were strictly notes, labs were super chill and fun

Dr. Simpson is clearly very knowledgeable but sometimes doesn't explain things in the way someone new to chemistry would understand. Class was not interactive and often boring. He tended to go off on tangents about things we didn't need to know for the class. He was a great facilitator in lab though.
Dr. Simpson is a much better lab instructor than a lecturer. He is helpful and if you do all of the pre-lab work and respond well to feedback, it will be fine
Dr. Simpson is not the best lecturer. As the semester continues you kind of lose him and is hard to keep up. However he is easy to reach outside of class and will help a lot

This class was a pretty normal lecture. He went through slides and added in some jokes. The class was not very interactive and I was often zoned out. He also tended to go off on tangents on things that we did not actually need to know for the class and would skim over things that could have used more instructional time. He is generally very chill.

Dr. Simpson is an excellent chemistry lab instructor. He clearly explains the lab steps (assuming you have completed all the pre-lab work, don't skip that) .His only flaw is that he sometimes answers simple questions with too much detail, making it a bit hard to follow, but the information is always relevant.

Quizzes are generally easy up until the last few but he drops the lowest one. Do the practice problems! He gets test questions from them. No midterm and final was super accessible. His lectures can be kinda dry but he cracks lots of jokes to offset it. Definitely go to his office hours, he'll work through every problem with you.

It's important to take notes during the start of lab lectures to understand the workshop. That being said, he is a very patient and understanding person and will individually explain it to you multiple times. I've been in his labs for two semesters now and I've never regretted being honest with him about why i missed a deadline.
This professor does not even understand what he's talking about. The class is lecture-based and is super boring. Quizzes are not so hard.

I had Dr. Simpson for 141 and 205 lab, and he is the best professor I've had at UR. He cares about his students and wants them to do well in class. He is always willing to help (even during quizzes/exams). The homework is almost identical to the quizzes. For the 205 lab, he helped with the reports, explaining in detail.

Take Dr. Simpson for class!
A very calm professor, who makes the lab environment not stressful. Clearly passionate about his work. Approachable and kind

Dr. Simpson was great and really cares to make sure students know the material. He's always willing to answer questions and gives a lot of partial credit on tests and quizzes. He also makes really good coffee cake and brownies!
This man gave me half credit on a true or false question... enough said.

KING. The nicest guy ever and truly cares for his students. So willing to help about literally anything and will answer questions on tests. His lectures are sometimes a little dry but he does his best to spice it up with his nerdy humor. Any class Jeff teaches, I would consider taking. (He also makes the best coffee cake!!) Take his class.

Very good in his Chem 141 course, explained and went over a lot of the practice problems. That being said, you should definitely read the text ahead of time to better understand some of the concepts (mostly the later chapters.)

I really enjoyed having Dr. Simpson for lab. He was clear and concise with his pre-lab lectures, and once we started working on the lab work he was always extremely helpful if we had a question or needed help.

Simpson lectures for almost every class and although its usually boring, pay attention and take notes because it will help with the hw. If you don't understand the hw, go to office hours and he will work through them with you! The hw is normally harder than the exams and graded on accuracy. Don't bother buying textbook but do practice problems

Dr. Simpson is a very understanding and helpful professor; any questions you have he will answer over email, in office hours, and even during a quiz or test. Practice problems were always provided for extra help (oftentimes he uses these questions on assessments). If you pay attention and do the homework, it isn't hard to do well in this class.

Dr. Simpson is a great/caring professor. He's very lenient with his grading and offers partial credit on his quizzes which are exactly like the practice problems that he gives out. He's reachable outside of class. He also makes a  good coffee cake. Reading the textbook is recommended but not necessary. Do the practice work and you'll be fine.

Dr. Simpson is a very nice professor. He wants you to succeed and helps in anyway he can. He gives practice questions that are almost exactly the quizzes. Throughout the yar we had 6 quizzes, a midterm and a final. He lectures for most of class and sometimes lets the class out early. He is too smart for intro chem.

Dr. Simpson's lectures are fun and engaging. He provides practice problems that are often the exact questions on quizzes and exams and gives curves when necessary. He is accessible outside of class and will help you with the homework, giving you the correct answers. You can really tell how much Dr. Simpson wants to see his students succeed.

Dr. Simpson is very clear and helpful in the way he explains chemistry concepts. He keeps his lectures engaging by giving random fun facts about the content that sometimes are just so unrelated but it's fun. He's accessible and doesn't give an unnecessary amount of work. If you're a textbook person, read the textbook, but I didn't and did fine.

Simpson was a great professor who clearly wanted to see his students succeed. He added humor to his lectures and was always available for outside help. While the course material is hard, he explains topics well and I would definitely take another class of his.
Makes class interesting, adds humor to his lectures, is frequently available to meet with students, and often gives partial credit. Is clearly interested in helping his students succeed.

Professor Simpson is a nice guy. Lectures are boring and fast paced; keeping up can be difficult if you didn't take AP chem. He is SUPER accessible outside of class and is always willing to answer questions about the HW. He is also very helpful during quizzes. My block had a few quizzes, a midterm, and a final. If you do the work, you will get an A

I had Simpson for CHEM 111 lab and he was really cool. His pre lab lectures were helpful, but I think he sometimes assumed we were all chem majors because he would turn us loose with no idea of how to use the majority of instruments in the class. Otherwise, he gives a lot of helpful feedback on lab reports.
I had Jeff for chem 141 lab and he was great. Made it super clear what he expected and answered all questions

Having never taken AP Chem I was anxious about entering Chem 141. While his lectures are sometimes confusing, all of the homework comes from the textbook so a lot of answers can be found online. Tests are very reasonable. He is easy to talk with, and if you show effort, you will get an A. I would take this class again. Jeff is great.

Super nice guy who always tries his best to explain and seems very willing to help students. For someone who hasn't taken chemistry before, it might be a little difficult because the class does move very quickly

Lab Experience: Dr. Simpson is alright. Since he was a lab prof, there was more for him to supervise than to teach. BUT he would help you if you asked. Sure, explanations arent always clear, but hell rephrase and reword until you get it. Willing to meet outside of class. lenient with a COUPLE of late works/grades. Not always careful with comments

Super nicest helpful guy but not the best teacher. You can tell he knows what hes talking about but he just doesnt know exactly how to break it down and give the basics to someone just learning the topic. Gave homework problems from the textbook every class and a quiz (which was always way harder than the homework) like every two weeks.

Very nice guy! Helpful with homework questions. Definitely had to read the textbook a lot, but overall the quizzes and final were doable. Learned lots from this class! He is a great lab professor as well.

He isn't the best professor but isn't the worst either. His lectures are really boring and is hard to stay concentrated -- especially if you have a 9 am. So, you pretty much need to read the entire chapter by yourself. Although, he is really accessible outside of class. Homework everyday and divides a test into two quizzes which are fairly easy.

Jeff is a great person and a helpful professor. His lectures are a little on the boring side but they are manageable. Be prepared to read a lot outside of class though, since there are times where he doesnt cover everything. Jeff really wants to see you succeed. He will always respond to your emails and does his absolute best to answer questions
